2607.28513.title: Creative Transformation in Literary Texts: Modelling Change Across Representational Levels
2607.28513.paper_summary: Creativity is often framed as the production of novelty, yet many cultural works emerge through transformation of earlier artifacts and not through isolated invention. Drawing on theories of imitation by Gabriel Tarde and James Mark Baldwin, this paper models creativity as selective transformation across multiple levels of textual representation. We introduce a multi-level framework that compares literary texts across lexical, semantic, conceptual, structural, and narrative dimensions using directional alignment and control calibrated similarity measures. Applying the model to historically documented literary relationships, we show that different pairs preserve source structure at different representational levels while diverging in others. These transformation profiles provide a quantitative method for characterizing how imitation persists and where creative divergence occurs within literary works.
2607.28513.paper_summary_zh: 創造力常常被框架為新穎性的產出，然而許多文化作品是通過對早期文物的轉化而產生，而非孤立的發明。本文借鑒了加布里埃爾·塔爾德和詹姆斯·馬克·鮑德溫的模仿理論，將創造力建模為在多個文本表現層次上的選擇性轉化。我們引入了一個多層次框架，通過方向性對齊和控制校準的相似性度量，對詞彙、語義、概念、結構和敘事維度上的文學文本進行比較。將該模型應用於歷史記錄的文學關係，我們顯示出不同的配對在不同的表現層次上保留了來源結構，同時在其他方面出現了分歧。這些轉化特徵提供了一種定量方法，用於描述模仿如何持續存在以及在文學作品中創造性分歧出現的位置。
2607.28513.author: Ioana-Roxana Boriceanu et.al.
